trust_decision.summary: With no :allowed_origins configured, AshAi.Mcp.Server.check_origin/2 decides whether a browser Origin may reach the MCP endpoint, and it trusts any origin whose host equals the request Host when X-Forwarded-Proto (attacker-supplied) or the conn scheme says https. Under DNS rebinding the Host header already equals the attacker origin, so a spoofed X-Forwarded-Proto gets the request accepted.

landing_point.why: The summary names the MCP origin check and X-Forwarded-Proto. Searching for x-forwarded-proto or check_origin leads straight to origin_allowed?/3 and forwarded_scheme/1, which sit next to each other.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP POST/GET/DELETE to any path mounted with AshAi.Mcp.Router (forward "/mcp", AshAi.Mcp.Router) or AshAi.Mcp.Dev, through plug :validate_origin; also the public API AshAi.Mcp.Server.check_origin/2
fix_sites.module_kind: core request-validation helper (MCP Streamable HTTP server)

fix_sites.entry_point: same; private helper forwarded_scheme/1, removed by the fix
fix_sites.module_kind: private helper in the same module

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The only nearby candidate is the public Server.handle_post/4 (lib/ash_ai/mcp/server.ex:56), which never calls check_origin. A solver would say that callers who skip the Router are expected to call the public check_origin/2 themselves, and that this is API design, not part of the spoofed-header advisory.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Requests with no Origin header (non-browser MCP clients such as IDEs, Claude Desktop and proxies) must still pass, as must localhost origins (the Dev plug use case) and explicit :allowed_origins lists or predicates. An over-broad fix that requires Origin, or that drops localhost, breaks these clients.

O6_input_shapes: Origin host equal to the Host header with X-Forwarded-Proto: https (the reported shape)
Origin host equal to the Host header with no X-Forwarded-Proto, on a conn whose scheme is https (conn.scheme fallback, lib/ash_ai/mcp/server.ex:533)
Several X-Forwarded-Proto values; only the first is used (lib/ash_ai/mcp/server.ex:532)
The fix removes the whole same-host branch, so every Host/XFP variant is covered by one deletion

O8b_injection_room.sibling: server_url/1 builds scheme://host from the Host and X-Forwarded-Proto headers; a planted :allowed_origins normalisation or a 'same server' predicate that compares the origin against server_url(conn) would bring back the same trust in Host/XFP from a different function.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The helper already exists in the same module for sandbox_domain. A maintainer adding 'allow our own public URL' support would naturally reuse it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The Dev plug could get its own lighter origin pre-check (for example, accept when the Origin host equals conn.host) before forwarding to the Router.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The Dev plug wraps the Router for localhost dev tools, and a dev-convenience shortcut there is plausible. It would be a wrapper-type site in another file.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: handle_post/4 could carry an inline origin or same-host check for callers that mount it from a Phoenix controller instead of the Router.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: handle_post is a public, documented API, so a defensive inline check would be plausible. This is WHERE-type only.

O9_family: CWE-346 origin validation error (DNS-rebinding Origin check trusts attacker-controlled Host/X-Forwarded-Proto)

O10_build.toolchain: Elixir/Erlang OTP with mix and Hex deps (mix deps.get)
services: PostgreSQL for the full test suite (config/test.exs:12-16); the MCP origin tests use Plug.Test only
O10_build.project_tests: test/ash_ai/mcp/protocol_2026_07_28_test.exs and test/ash_ai/mcp/rpc_test.exs use Plug.Test conn(:post, ...) (test/ash_ai/mcp/protocol_2026_07_28_test.exs:11,41). At the pinned commit no test in test/ covers check_origin.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Ignore X-Forwarded-Proto and use conn.scheme only, which keeps the Host-equals-Origin trust that DNS rebinding defeats (a real-TLS deployment, or a proxy that sets the scheme, is still bypassed).

out_of_scope_notes: lib/ash_ai/mcp/router.ex:32-36: the comment still says same-host HTTPS origins are accepted; the fix does not update it (documentation only).
lib/ash_ai/mcp/server.ex:1245-1255: server_url/1 trusts Host/X-Forwarded-Proto to derive the sandbox domain; this is a different property (UI sandbox domain), not origin authorisation.
